mock_data.title: More Break-ins
mock_data.passage:
Once again, there has been a series of robberies in the town. This week several homes have been broken into in Robertson Street and residents are both worried and angry. 'Something must be done about this now,' said 58-year-old Jack Clements. 'It's time the police got their finger out and caught these villains. A lot of elderly people live around here and they're terrified.'

A police spokesman told us, 'We are doing all in our power to catch the people who are responsible for these burglaries. The police are stretched to breaking point in this town. Because of budgetary requirements we have made drastic reductions in the number of police officers on the beat and this at a time when we are faced with a rising tide of crime, especially among young people.'

Said Dick Rogers, 64, another resident of Robertson Street, 'The government should put its money where its mouth is. They're always going on about the importance of law and order, but we still don't have nearly enough police. We used to have a police force that was in a class by itself, but now we hear of nothing but cutbacks.'

Mary Roberts, 67, also a resident of Robertson Street, said, 'It's a sign of the times that these crimes are being committed by young people. It's just part and parcel of their general attitude. They're no longer afraid of anyone in authority and have no respect for other people or their property. If we catch any of them around here breaking into houses we'll give them what for, I promise you.'

Inspector James Rowland sympathized with the concern of the Robertson Street residents, but urged them not to take the law into their own hands. 'If you do see someone breaking in, get in touch with us immediately. Don't be tempted to have a go or you could end up being badly injured. We have a lot of officers working on these burglaries at the moment, but up till now we have not made any arrests. We are, however, following up a few lines of enquiry, although we are obviously not in a position at this stage to name names. Meanwhile, we would ask all members of the public to be vigilant and to report anything suspicious to the police.'
mock_data.passageB1:
There have been more break-ins in our town. This week, some houses in Robertson Street were broken into. People who live there are worried and angry.

Jack Clements, who is 58, said, "We need to do something now! The police need to catch these criminals. Many older people live here, and they are very scared."

A police spokesman said, "We are trying our best to catch the people who did these break-ins. The police have a lot of work in this town. We have fewer police officers because we have less money. At the same time, there is more crime, especially among young people."

Dick Rogers, 64, who also lives on Robertson Street, said, "The government should spend money on the police. They always talk about law and order, but we don't have enough police officers. We used to have a very good police force, but now there are only cutbacks."

Mary Roberts, 67, who also lives on Robertson Street, said, "It's common now for young people to do these crimes. They don't respect anyone in charge, or other people's things. If we see them breaking into houses, we will teach them a lesson!"

Inspector James Rowland said he understood the people in Robertson Street were concerned. But he told them not to take the law into their own hands. "If you see someone breaking in, call us right away. Don't try to stop them yourself, because you could get hurt. We have many officers working on these break-ins, but we have not arrested anyone yet. We are investigating some clues, but we can't say any names now. Please, everyone, be careful and tell the police if you see anything suspicious."
mock_data.passageB2:
The town is once again experiencing a spate of burglaries, with several homes on Robertson Street being targeted this week. Residents are understandably on edge, expressing both worry and anger. Jack Clements, a 58-year-old resident, voiced the community's frustration: 'Something needs to be done immediately. It's time the police stepped up their efforts and apprehended these criminals. Many elderly individuals live in this area and are living in constant fear.'

A police spokesperson acknowledged the residents' concerns, stating, 'We are doing everything within our power to catch those responsible for these crimes. However, the police force is currently under immense pressure. Due to budget cuts, we've had to make significant reductions in the number of officers on patrol, which is happening at a time when we are seeing a rise in crime, particularly among young people.'

Dick Rogers, 64, another resident of Robertson Street, believes the government needs to back up their words with actions. 'They constantly talk about the importance of law and order, yet we still don't have enough police officers. We once had an excellent police force, but now all we hear about are cutbacks.'

Mary Roberts, 67, also a Robertson Street resident, commented on the social factors possibly at play. 'It's a sad reflection of our times that these crimes are being committed by young people. It seems to be part of their general attitude. They no longer respect authority and show no regard for other people or their property. If we catch any of them trying to break into houses around here, we'll give them a piece of our mind, I assure you.'

Inspector James Rowland acknowledged the residents' anxiety but cautioned them against taking matters into their own hands. 'If you witness a break-in, please contact us immediately. Do not attempt to intervene directly, as you could risk serious injury. We have a number of officers actively investigating these burglaries, but so far, no arrests have been made. We are, however, pursuing several leads, although we cannot reveal specific details at this stage. In the meantime, we urge all members of the public to remain vigilant and report any suspicious activity to the police.'
mock_data.passageC1:
A fresh spate of burglaries has once again cast a pall over the residents of our town. This week alone, several homes on Robertson Street have been targeted, leaving homeowners in a state of heightened anxiety and simmering resentment. As 58-year-old Jack Clements articulated, 'Decisive action is now of paramount importance. It's high time the police pulled their socks up and apprehended these criminals. The area is home to a significant number of elderly individuals, and they are understandably living in fear.'

A police spokesperson acknowledged the community's concerns, stating, 'We are exerting every effort to bring the perpetrators of these burglaries to justice. However, the constabulary is currently operating under immense strain. Due to budgetary constraints, we have been compelled to implement significant reductions in frontline officers, a situation which coincides with a discernible upswing in criminal activity, particularly among the youth.' The spokesperson stopped short of providing specifics on the ongoing investigation.

Dick Rogers, 64, another resident of the beleaguered Robertson Street, expressed his frustration, asserting, 'The government needs to translate its rhetoric into action. They are constantly professing the importance of law and order, yet we remain critically under-resourced in terms of policing. We once boasted a police force that was second to none, but now we are perpetually confronted with news of further cutbacks. It's a downward spiral.'

Mary Roberts, 67, also a resident, offered a societal perspective, 'These crimes committed by young people are symptomatic of a broader malaise. They are indicative of a pervasive attitude of disregard for authority and a lack of respect for both individuals and their property. Should we apprehend any of them attempting to break into houses in this vicinity, they will face the consequences, you can be sure of that.' She spoke with unfeigned anger.

Inspector James Rowland, while sympathizing with the palpable apprehension of the Robertson Street residents, strongly cautioned against any attempts at vigilante justice. 'Should you witness a break-in, please contact us immediately. Resist the temptation to intervene, as you could potentially sustain serious injuries. We have dedicated a considerable number of officers to these burglaries, and while we have yet to make any arrests, we are pursuing several promising leads. Naturally, we are not at liberty to disclose specific details at this juncture. In the interim, we urge all members of the public to maintain vigilance and to report any suspicious activity to the police without delay. We are working to restore a sense of security to the area.' He also cautioned against jumping to conclusions about the perpetrators' identities.

questions.answer: The passage is expected to be about a series of robberies or break-ins in a local area, as reported by a local newspaper. It will likely include information about where they occurred, reactions from residents and/or police, and possibly details about the crimes.
questions.question: From the title and subtitle above, what do you expect the passage to be about?

questions.answer: Answers may vary. Common information sought: where and when it happened, what was stolen, if anyone was hurt, whether suspects were caught, police statements, witness accounts, how the burglars entered, what precautions people should take, if it's part of a pattern.
questions.question: When you read a newspaper report about a robbery, what information are you looking for?

questions.answer: Answers may vary. Reasons include: poverty and financial need, drug addiction, unemployment, opportunity (easy targets), lack of security, organized crime, desperation, greed, peer pressure, societal inequality, lack of education/opportunities, thrill-seeking.

mock_data.translation:
Yana bir marta shaharda bir qator o'g'irliklar sodir bo'ldi. Bu hafta Robertson ko'chasida bir nechta uyga bostirib kirildi va aholi ham tashvishda, ham g'azablangan. "Bu haqda hozir nimadir qilinishi kerak," dedi 58 yoshli Jek Klements. "Politsiya barmoqlarini chiqarish va bu yovuzlarni ushlash vaqti keldi. Bu atrofda ko'plab qariyalar yashaydi va ular vahimaga tushgan."

Politsiya vakili bizga aytdi: "Biz bu o'g'irliklarga javobgar bo'lgan odamlarni ushlash uchun qo'limizdan kelganining hammasini qilyapmiz. Politsiya bu shaharda sinish nuqtasigacha cho'zilgan. Budjet talablari tufayli biz patrul xizmatidagi politsiya xodimlarining sonini keskin qisqartirdik va bu bizga yoshlar o'rtasida ayniqsa jinoyatlarning ko'payib borayotgan to'lqini bilan yuzma-yuz bo'layotgan bir paytda."

Robertson ko'chasining yana bir aholisi 64 yoshli Dik Rojers dedi: "Hukumat pulini og'ziga qo'yishi kerak. Ular doimo qonun va tartib muhimligi haqida gapiradilar, ammo bizda hali ham deyarli yetarli politsiya yo'q. Bizda o'zining sinfida turgan politsiya kuchlari bor edi, ammo endi faqat qisqartirishlar haqida eshitamiz."

Robertson ko'chasida yashovchi 67 yoshli Meri Roberts aytdi: "Bu jinoyatlarni yoshlar tomonidan sodir etilishi zamonning belgisi. Bu ularning umumiy munosabatining bir qismi va paketining bir qismi. Ular endi hokimiyatdagi hech kimdan qo'rqmaydilar va boshqa odamlarga yoki ularning mulkiga hurmat ko'rsatmaydilar. Agar biz ulardan birontasini bu atrofda uylarga bostirib kirayotganida ushlab qolsak, biz ularga nima uchun ekanligini ko'rsatamiz, sizga va'da beraman."

Inspektor Jeyms Rouland Robertson ko'chasi aholisining tashvishiga hamdard bo'ldi, ammo ularni qonunni o'z qo'llariga olmaslikka chaqirdi. "Agar siz kimningdir bostirib kirganini ko'rsangiz, darhol biz bilan bog'laning. Harakat qilishga vasvasalanmang, aks holda siz og'ir jarohatlangan bo'lishingiz mumkin. Bizda hozirda bu o'g'irliklar ustida ishlaydigan ko'plab xodimlar bor, ammo hozirgacha biz hech qanday hibsga olmadik. Biroq, biz bir nechta tergov yo'nalishlarini kuzatib boryapmiz, garchi bu bosqichda nomlarni aytish holatida emasligimiz aniq. Shu bilan birga, biz jamoatchilikni hushyor bo'lishga va politsiyaga shubhali narsalarni xabar qilishga chaqiramiz."

mock_data.translationB1:
Bizning shahrimizda uy o'g'irliklari ko'paydi. Bu hafta Robertson ko'chasidagi ba'zi uylarga o'g'irlik tushdi. U yerda yashovchi odamlar xavotirda va jahldor.

58 yoshli Jek Klements shunday dedi: "Hozir biror narsa qilishimiz kerak! Politsiya bu jinoyatchilarni qo'lga olishi kerak. Bu yerda ko'plab keksa odamlar yashaydi va ular juda qo'rqishadi."

Politsiya vakili shunday dedi: "Biz bu uy o'g'irliklarini qilgan odamlarni qo'lga olish uchun qo'limizdan kelganicha harakat qilyapmiz. Politsiyaning bu shaharda ishi ko'p. Bizda pul kamligi sababli politsiya xodimlari kam. Shu bilan birga, jinoyatchilik, ayniqsa yoshlar orasida, ko'paymoqda."

Robertson ko'chasida yashovchi 64 yoshli Dik Rojers shunday dedi: "Hukumat politsiyaga pul sarflashi kerak. Ular doimo qonun va tartib haqida gapirishadi, lekin bizda yetarli politsiya xodimlari yo'q. Ilgari bizda juda yaxshi politsiya kuchlari bor edi, lekin hozir faqat qisqartirishlar bor."

Robertson ko'chasida yashovchi 67 yoshli Meri Roberts shunday dedi: "Hozir yoshlarning bu jinoyatlarni qilishi odatiy hol. Ular hech kimni, boshliqlarni ham, boshqalarning narsalarini ham hurmat qilishmaydi. Agar ularning uylarga o'g'irlik tushayotganini ko'rsak, biz ularga sabog'ini beramiz!"

Inspektor Jeyms Rouland Robertson ko'chasidagi odamlarning xavotirlarini tushunishini aytdi. Ammo u ularga qonunni o'z qo'llariga olmaslikni aytdi. "Agar kimningdir o'g'irlik qilayotganini ko'rsangiz, darhol bizga qo'ng'iroq qiling. Ularni o'zingiz to'xtatishga urinmang, chunki siz jarohat olishingiz mumkin. Bizning ko'plab xodimlarimiz bu uy o'g'irliklari ustida ishlamoqda, lekin biz hali hech kimni hibsga olganimiz yo'q. Biz ba'zi dalillarni tekshirmoqdamiz, lekin hozir hech qanday ism ayta olmaymiz. Iltimos, hammangiz ehtiyot bo'ling va agar biron bir shubhali narsani ko'rsangiz, politsiyaga xabar bering."
mock_data.translationB2:
Shaharda yana o‘g‘irlik holatlari avj olmoqda, xususan, bu hafta Robertson ko‘chasidagi bir nechta uylar nishonga olindi. Mahalliy aholi juda xavotirda, tashvish va g‘azabini bildirishmoqda. 58 yoshli mahalliy aholi vakili Jek Klements jamiyatning noroziligini quyidagicha ifoda etdi: 'Zudlik bilan chora ko‘rish kerak. Politsiya harakatlarini kuchaytirishi va bu jinoyatchilarni qo‘lga olishi kerak. Bu hududda ko‘plab keksa odamlar yashaydi va ular doimiy qo‘rquvda yashashmoqda.'

Politsiya vakili mahalliy aholining xavotirlarini tan olib, shunday dedi: 'Biz bu jinoyatlar uchun mas'ul bo'lganlarni ushlash uchun qo'limizdan kelganicha harakat qilmoqdamiz. Biroq, hozirda politsiya kuchlariga katta bosim o'tkazilmoqda. Budjet qisqarishi tufayli biz patrulda bo'lgan ofitserlar sonini sezilarli darajada kamaytirishga majbur bo'ldik, bu esa ayniqsa yoshlar orasida jinoyatchilikning ko'payishini kuzatayotgan paytga to'g'ri kelmoqda.'

Robertson ko'chasining yana bir aholisi, 64 yoshli Dik Rojersning fikricha, hukumat gapini amalda isbotlashi kerak. 'Ular doimiy ravishda qonun va tartibning muhimligi haqida gapirishadi, ammo bizda hali ham yetarli politsiya xodimlari yo'q. Bir paytlar bizda ajoyib politsiya kuchlari bor edi, ammo hozir biz faqat qisqartirishlar haqida eshitamiz.'

Robertson ko'chasining yana bir aholisi, 67 yoshli Meri Roberts, ehtimol ta'sir o'tkazayotgan ijtimoiy omillar haqida izoh berdi. 'Bu jinoyatlar yoshlar tomonidan sodir etilayotgani bizning zamonamizning achinarli aksidir. Bu ularning umumiy munosabatining bir qismi bo'lib tuyuladi. Ular endi hokimiyatni hurmat qilishmaydi va boshqa odamlarga yoki ularning mol-mulkiga hech qanday e'tibor berishmaydi. Agar biz ulardan birontasini bu yerda uylarga o'g'irlik qilishga urinayotganini ushlasak, biz ularga qattiq gapiramiz, ishonch hosil qiling.'

Inspektor Jeyms Roulend mahalliy aholining xavotirlarini tan oldi, ammo ularni masalani o'z qo'llariga olishdan ogohlantirdi. 'Agar siz o'g'irlikni ko'rsangiz, darhol biz bilan bog'laning. To'g'ridan-to'g'ri aralashishga urinmang, chunki siz jiddiy jarohat olishingiz mumkin. Bizda bu o'g'irliklarni faol ravishda tekshirayotgan bir qator ofitserlar bor, ammo hozircha hech kim hibsga olinmagan. Biroq, biz bir nechta yo'nalishlarni o'rganmoqdamiz, garchi biz bu bosqichda aniq tafsilotlarni oshkor qila olmasak ham. Shu bilan birga, biz barcha fuqarolarni hushyor bo'lishga va har qanday shubhali faoliyat haqida politsiyaga xabar berishga chaqiramiz.'

Yangi o'g'irliklar to'lqini yana bir bor shaharimiz aholisining ustiga qora soya soldi. Faqat shu hafta ichida Robertson ko'chasidagi bir nechta uylar nishonga olindi, bu esa uy egalarini kuchaygan xavotir va yashirin norozilik holatiga tushirdi. 58 yoshli Jek Klements ta'kidlaganidek, 'Hozirda hal qiluvchi choralar ko'rish nihoyatda muhim. Politsiya astoydil harakat qilib, bu jinoyatchilarni qo'lga olishi kerak. Bu hududda qariyalarning soni ko'p va ular tushunarli ravishda qo'rquvda yashamoqda.'

Politsiya vakili jamiyatning xavotirlarini tan olib, shunday dedi: 'Biz ushbu o'g'irlik jinoyatchilarini adolatga tortish uchun bor kuchimizni sarflayapmiz. Biroq, politsiya hozirda juda katta bosim ostida ishlamoqda. Budjet cheklovlari tufayli biz oldingi saflardagi xodimlarni sezilarli darajada qisqartirishga majbur bo'ldik, bu holat esa jinoyatchilik faolligining sezilarli darajada oshishi bilan bir vaqtga to'g'ri keldi, ayniqsa yoshlar orasida.' Vakil davom etayotgan tergov bo'yicha aniq ma'lumot berishdan tiyildi.

Robertson ko'chasining yana bir jabrlanuvchi aholisi, 64 yoshli Dik Rojers o'zining noroziligini bildirib, shunday dedi: 'Hukumat o'z gaplarini amaliy harakatga aylantirishi kerak. Ular doimo qonun va tartibning muhimligini ta'kidlashadi, ammo biz politsiya xodimlari nuqtai nazaridan juda kam resurslarga egamiz. Biz bir vaqtlar hech kimdan kam bo'lmagan politsiya kuchiga ega edik, ammo hozir doimo qisqartirishlar haqidagi xabarlarga duch kelamiz. Bu pastga qarab harakatlanish.'

Shuningdek, shu hududda yashovchi 67 yoshli Meri Roberts jamiyat nuqtai nazarini bildirdi: 'Yoshlar tomonidan sodir etilgan bu jinoyatlar kengroq bir dardning belgisi. Ular hokimiyatga bepisand munosabatda bo'lishning va shaxslarga hamda ularning mulkiga hurmat yo'qligining dalilidir. Agar biz ulardan birortasini shu atrofda uylarga o'g'irlik qilishga urinayotganini ushlasak, ular oqibatlariga duch kelishadi, bunga ishonchingiz komil bo'lsin.' U samimiy g'azab bilan gapirdi.

Inspektor Jeyms Rouland Robertson ko'chasi aholisining sezilarli xavotiriga hamdardlik bildirgan holda, o'zboshimchalik bilan adolat o'rnatishga urinmaslik haqida qattiq ogohlantirdi. 'Agar siz o'g'irlikni ko'rsangiz, darhol bizga xabar bering. Aralashish vasvasasiga qarshi turing, chunki siz jiddiy jarohatlar olishingiz mumkin. Biz bu o'g'irliklar uchun ko'p sonli xodimlarni ajratdik va biz hali hech kimni hibsga olmagan bo'lsak ham, biz bir nechta istiqbolli yo'nalishlarni kuzatib bormoqdamiz. Tabiiyki, biz hozircha aniq tafsilotlarni oshkor qilishga haqli emasmiz. Shu bilan birga, biz barcha fuqarolarni hushyor bo'lishga va har qanday shubhali faoliyat haqida politsiyaga kechiktirmasdan xabar berishga chaqiramiz. Biz hududda xavfsizlik hissini tiklash uchun ishlayapmiz.' U, shuningdek, jinoyatchilarning shaxsiga oid xulosalar chiqarishga shoshilmaslik haqida ogohlantirdi.
